claims.statement: A requirement has only two true states, `open` and `done`; `split`, `merged` and `dropped` are `closed_reason` values, so the nine displayed stages are a projection over `plan_ok`, `job`, `gate` and `integrating` rather than stored states.

The executor ledger records which subagent id ran which stage of which requirement; switching id across a stage boundary needs an explicit `<new_id>|<reason>`, and placeholder ids are filtered out of resume decisions.

A dispatched job carries a self-contained `subagentAction` (brief, deltaPrompt, fullFallbackBrief, worktreePath, artifactPath, submitCommand), which is what lets any harness adapter run the lane without reimplementing the workflow.
Lanes form a bounded persistent pool of git worktrees; claiming resets the branch to `HEAD` while keeping untracked build caches, and releasing parks on detached `HEAD` so no branch is ever locked.
Run artifacts live in an in-archive VFS table inside `run.sqlite`, addressed as `artifacts/*` and exposed to Lua through `ygg.fs.*` with SHA-256 integrity.

The tools registry is self-declared through `config.set tools.*`: `tools.root` acts as the machine-evidence switch, session keys carry the main-session identity because the sandbox cannot read process env, and an unregistered tool is a readable refusal at its consumption point.

A run has two states, `live` and `retired`, with `charter`, coordinate, `settle` and `release` as micro-phases; retirement is reachable only when `run.retire` armed the run, so requirement `done` and run `retired` are homonyms rather than the same concept.
A stable checkpoint is the only point where context compaction and a structured handover are safe, because in-flight subagent output is not otherwise recoverable.
